verdict: EDGE DOES NOT SURVIVE REAL-MARKET COSTS

phase19_real_market_test.conditions: SYNTHETIC POLYMARKET DATA WITH REALISTIC COSTS

cost_model_applied.notes: Conservative estimates; real costs may be lower in liquid markets

root_cause_analysis.conclusion: Costs are 22× larger than the edge. Signal is mathematically unable to overcome friction.
root_cause_analysis.key_insight: Problem is structural, not parametric. Not solvable by optimization.

q1_beats_random.question: Does signal beat random on real data?

q2_edge_survives_costs.question: Edge reduced but not eliminated by costs?

q4_k3_adds_value.question: K3 still adds value in real conditions?

option_1_abandon.rationale: Most retail directional trading fails; mean reversion needs higher edges

option_2_redesign_larger_moves.description: Find signals that trigger at ±5-10% scales
option_2_redesign_larger_moves.rationale: Larger moves can overcome costs, but rare in prediction markets

option_3_cost_reduction.description: Test on extremely liquid pairs, optimize for lower costs
option_3_cost_reduction.rationale: Costs rarely drop below 100 bps round-trip; unlikely to solve problem

conclusion: Phase 19 conclusively demonstrates that the A_MOMENTUM_REVERSAL edge does NOT survive real-market conditions. The signal achieves 53.6% win rate in frictionless simulation, but this edge is entirely consumed by realistic trading costs (320 bps round-trip). The strategy is mathematically unviable.
